contract: These are the only colour, type, spacing, radius, border, shadow, motion and z-index values that may appear in generated markup or CSS. A value not listed here is a design-system gap: report it, do not invent one. Raw colour literals are permitted in exactly one file, tokens/palette.css.

--r-0.note: * * border-radius tokens * * Corner radius scale. * * Numeric, matching the spacing convention. The semantic --r-4/md/lg * aliases were removed for the same reason as --space-*. * * Generated-adjacent: tokens/tokens.json is derived from this folder by * `node ui/scripts/gen-tokens.mjs`. Editing a value here means regenerating it.

--r-full.note: Pill/circle. Was referenced as --r-full in three places and declared nowhere, so not-defined.css's skeleton avatar computed border-radius:0 — a square placeholder for a round element.

--bw-1.note: border_width.dart defines hairline(0.5)/thin(1)/base(2)/thick(3)/ thicker(4) — only thin/base existed here. --bw-4 mirrors thicker(4); its original consumer (app-card's left accent bar) is gone, so it has none right now. hairline/thick are still gaps if a component needs them.

--shell-bg.note: * * colour tokens — semantic * * What components actually reference. Every value here resolves to a ramp step * in palette.css, usually through light-dark() so one name serves both themes. * * Four groups: * 1. Shell chrome — the ink plane. Deliberately NOT theme-switched. * 2. Semantic — --bg-* / --fg-* / --border-*. The main vocabulary. * 3. Syntax — code highlighting. * 4. Legacy aliases — --color-* kept so old component CSS re-skins unchanged. * Do not use in new code. * * No raw colour values. See palette.css.

--shell-fg-muted.note: sand-500, not white@62%: the ink plane is warm (#242628 family), and a cool grey glyph read as a different palette beside the gold selected state.

--shell-fg-error.note: Trouble, said on the ink plane. --fg-error and --fg-warning are light-dark() pairs and resolve to their LIGHT value on a light page — red/600 and orange/600, which are mixed for contrast against white and go muddy on sand/900. Chrome is dark in both themes (see group 1), so these are fixed at the dark-side steps the semantic roles already use there.

--bg-surface-subtle.note: Figma bg/default/surface-subtle (sand/200) — nested surfaces and secondary panels. Distinct from --bg-subtle above, which is a separate older name still referenced by --color-neutral-bg; do not merge them.

--fg-brand-strong.note: Brand text that has to be readable, not just brand-coloured: --fg-brand is yellow/600, which is 2.98:1 on a light surface — below AA for body text. This drops to yellow/800 (7.6:1) in light and keeps yellow/400 in dark, where the plain brand gold is already 12:1. Use it for brand-coloured *labels* (selected tab, brand link text); --fg-brand stays for accents, icons and rules where contrast is decorative.

--fg-icon-primary.note: Figma fg/default/icon-* — icons get their own roles because a secondary icon is brand-coloured while secondary *text* is sand/700.

--border-error-secondary.note: Figma border/default/error-secondary — the full-strength red outline on a destructive *secondary* button, distinct from the soft --border-error used for error surfaces.

--fg-constant-white.note: ── Constants and the dark notification overlay ────────────────────────── Figma's fg/constant and information-overlay roles. These deliberately do NOT use light-dark(): "constant" means the value is fixed regardless of theme (text on a brand pill is white in both), and the information-overlay plane is an always-dark floating surface, not a themed one. Wrapping either in light-dark() would invert it in dark mode and destroy the contrast the Figma spec annotates (fg/feedback/information-overlay is documented as 4.6:1 on sand/800). These three close the gap app-card.js records: its error-state "Know more" falls back to a native title tooltip because the inverse-surface tokens did not exist on the web side. They do now.

--chart-axis-label.note: ── Data-visualisation series ──────────────────────────────────────────── The categorical scale: identity, not magnitude. Slots are assigned in this fixed order and never cycled — colour follows the entity, so a filter that drops series 2 must not repaint series 3. An 8th series does NOT get a generated hue; it folds into "Other" (--fg-secondary). One set serves both themes. These are pastels, chosen to sit on the tinted chart panel, and unlike the rest of the palette they need no second dark-mode selection: they clear 3:1 against the dark surface as they stand. What that costs on the LIGHT panel, measured rather than guessed: contrast runs 1.1–2.2:1. That is the intended look for a filled mark whose value is written beside it, and it is why <app-chart> always ships a legend and direct labels — the relief that makes a sub-3:1 fill legible. It is thin for a 2px *line*, the one form where the pastel carries the reading alone. How far the scale actually stretches, by adjacent-pair separation under simulated deuteranopia and in normal vision: up to 5 series clean — worst pair ΔE 19.1 (deutan), 21.4 (normal) 6 series green/orange fall to ΔE 6.6 (deutan): legal only because every mark here is directly labelled 7 series orange/red are ΔE 9.3 in NORMAL vision — under the 15 floor, i.e. hard to tell apart for everyone No reordering fixes the 7-slot case (across all pairs, blue/purple are ΔE 1.3 under deuteranopia). Past five series the answer is a grouped "Other" bucket or small multiples, not more hues. Slots 6 and 7 are for palettes and swatches, not for a seven-series chart. Sequential (magnitude) and diverging (polarity) scales are deliberately absent — nothing needs one yet, and a ramp invented ahead of its first use is a ramp nobody validated. Chart chrome is mostly NOT here. Grid lines are --border-primary, an unfilled meter track is --bg-track — a chart is a surface like any other and does not get private greys. The one exception below is the axis/legend label ink, which the design names as its own decision (chart/axis/label, sand-700 in light) so a re-skin can change chart labelling without moving every body caption with it.

--color-bg-base.note: Page canvas / raised surfaces. --color-bg-base is the sand wash used for table heads, code wells, hovers. --color-bg-surface is the white plane cards / inputs sit on.

--bg-canvas-card.note: Chrome sitting directly on the ink shell (rare — most chrome is the shell itself)

--bg-input.note: Inputs are flat sand wells on the white plane — no stroke

--shadow-card-hover.note: * * elevation tokens * * Elevation. * * The design system is flat by default — borders carry depth. These exist * for the few surfaces that genuinely float (menus, hovered cards). * * Generated-adjacent: tokens/tokens.json is derived from this folder by * `node ui/scripts/gen-tokens.mjs`. Editing a value here means regenerating it.

--shadow-sm.note: Shadows — DS is flat; keep the legacy ramp shallow. light-dark() is a *color* function, so it wraps only the color — wrapping a whole shadow value (as this ramp used to) is invalid and computes to `none`, which silently dropped every shadow in the UI. Geometry is theme-independent.

--shadow-tooltip.note: Tooltips float above everything and are small, so they carry a tighter, darker shadow than a menu. Two values because the tooltip inverts against the light content plane. Extracted from app-tooltip's inline styles — the raw rgba() was the last hardcoded colour in design-system/.

--white.note: * * palette tokens — the raw ramps * * THE ONLY FILE IN THE CODEBASE WHERE A RAW COLOUR VALUE MAY BE WRITTEN. * `ui-lint`'s design-system-colors-are-tokens rule exempts this file by name * and nothing else, so a re-skin is exactly this file plus colors.css. * * Never reference a ramp step from a component. Components use the semantic * tokens in colors.css, which is what makes a re-skin mechanical.

--neutral-50.note: Ink neutral ramp — same hue family as --shell-bg (#242628) at ~5% saturation, NOT Tailwind Slate (~33% saturation on a blue hue). Dark surfaces come from light-dark(sand-*, neutral-*), so the old Slate values gave the whole dark theme a blue cast that clashed with the always-ink chrome. Two deliberate relationships: --neutral-800 (#2B2D30, the dark content surface) is slightly LIGHTER than the ink shell so the content plane floats above the chrome exactly as the white plane does in light theme, while --neutral-900 (#1A1C1E) is darker than the ink and serves as the recessed card/well surface sitting inside that plane.

--neutral-400.note: Lightened from #90949A: muted text on the dark plane measured 4.53:1 (AA with no headroom); this restores 5.24:1 at the same hue.

--sand-50.note: Warm sand ramp — NightOwl neutral scale (fig-tokens); the content plane, cards, inputs, and table chrome all read from this ramp

--sand-750.note: Figma calls this "sand/800+1": one step off sand-800, used only for dividers inside the dark notification drawer. Numbered 750 because the ramp runs light-to-dark and #4A4540 is lighter than --sand-800 (#3A3430).

--cream-50.note: Legacy warm cream canvas ramp — superseded by --sand-*, kept as aliases

--neutral-950.note: Darkest neutral. mcp-page.css referenced --neutral-950 with an inline `#0c0c0c` fallback because the ramp stopped at 900; declaring it removes the last raw hex from that file's dark-mode path.

--ink-control-hover.note: ==== Ink-plane chrome, and overlay tints ==== The shell is a fixed dark plane that does not theme-switch, so a couple of its fills have no equivalent step in the sand ramp. --overlay-* are the scrim tints behind modals: cool slate on purpose, so a scrim reads as "screen dimmed" rather than "warm surface".

--syntax-comment.note: ==== Syntax highlighting (GitHub-style) ==== A closed third-party palette, not ours to re-skin — it lives here because this is the one file allowed to hold raw values, not because it is part of the brand ramp.

--shell-topbar-height.note: * * sizing tokens * * Fixed sizes: icon boxes, control heights, shell and app chrome metrics. * * These are not spacing — they are the intrinsic size of a thing. * * Generated-adjacent: tokens/tokens.json is derived from this folder by * `node ui/scripts/gen-tokens.mjs`. Editing a value here means regenerating it.

--shell-gutter.note: The rail is the 32px button column only. It floats inside --shell-gutter on both sides, so the card's left edge lands at 12 + 32 + 12 = 56.

--s-0.note: --s-6 is NOT from spacing.dart: it is Figma's button/

--card-content-pad.note: Standard content padding inside the white card (52 top, 64 sides/bottom)

--lh-none.note: Leading + weight scale. Neither family existed, so every leading and weight in the component tree was a literal — which is why a type-scale change could not be mechanical.

--font-size-xs.note: Typography - Fluid sizing with clamp() (DS sizes carry the same clamps in Flutter: body 14–18, titles 36–44)

--font-size-sm.note: Body type — FIXED, from Figma "Design System V2" 7:532, same reason the button type below is fixed. Figma defines exactly two body ramps and both are viewport-independent: body/primary Inter 400 14/20 letter-spacing 0 (--font-size-base) body/secondary Inter 400 13/18 letter-spacing 0 (--font-size-sm) These were clamps (sm 12.8→14px, base 14.4→16px), so every body string in the app rendered one step above the design at desktop width.

--font-size-tertiary.note: body/tertiary Inter 400 12/16 — the third body ramp, added for the form controls (input hint + count rows, checkbox/radio/toggle subtext, and the sm input's own value text). NOT --font-size-xs: that is a clamp (11.2 → 12px) with existing consumers, so it resolves below the design at narrow widths. Fixed, for the same reason the two ramps above are.

--font-button-size.note: Button type — Figma font/buttons/* (7:532). Numerically equal to the body ramps above today, but kept as its own group because Figma models it as a separate variable set that can diverge. Labels also track --tracking-title.

--tracking-normal.note: Figma Font/Spacing/0 and Font/Spacing/Title. Titles and button labels track +0.16px; body tracks 0.

--font-display.value: 'Chivo Mono', ui-monospace, 'SF Mono', Menlo, Consolas, monospace

--font-mono.value: 'Chivo Mono', ui-monospace, 'SF Mono', Menlo, Consolas, monospace

--z-base.note: Stacking was eight hand-picked values from 0 to 10000 spread across five files, so "does this sit above that?" could only be answered by grepping. Named steps, deliberately sparse so there is room to insert between them. app-toast sits above app-modal on purpose: a toast confirming an action taken inside a dialog has to be readable while the dialog is still open.
